planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Cat's Cradle is a vigorous, well-branched spider daylily that reblooms over an extended early-to-midseason.

directions: Registered by Ben R. Hager in 1985, Cat's Cradle bears nocturnal, bright yellow spider-form blooms roughly 8 inches across on well-branched, 38-inch scapes, with a spider ratio exceeding 5.8:1. It flowers in the early-to-midseason and reblooms, extending the show well beyond a single flush. The cultivar won the AHS Harris Olson Spider Award in 1991, recognizing it as an outstanding example of the spider form class. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigorous bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained garden soil in full sun; Lois Burns is an early-blooming, reblooming spider daylily that stays evergreen in milder climates.

directions: Registered by Temple in 1986, Lois Burns carries large yellow-green spider blooms, around 8.5 inches across, with mango-toned streaking along the petal edges and a green throat, on 30-inch scapes. It flowers in the early season and reblooms later, and the diploid, evergreen plant is cold-hardy to about zone 5a. The cultivar earned the Harris Olson Spider Award as well as an Honorable Mention. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil and divide clumps every few years to keep bloom production strong.

common_name: Mountain Top Experience Daylily (Bicolor Spider Variant Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Mountain Top Experience is a recurved, extended-bloom spider variant that reblooms through the season.

directions: Registered by Temple in 1988, Mountain Top Experience is a bicolor spider variant (petal ratio 4.0:1 to 5.0:1) combining lavender-pink petals with pale orange-cream sepals around a purple chevron eyezone and green throat. Blooms open early in the season, recurve attractively, hold for an extended period, and rebloom later. The cultivar took the Harris Olson Spider Award and also received an Honorable Mention. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil and divide every three to four years to keep clumps productive.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; De Colores is a tall, wide-petaled spider daylily grown for its multi-toned bloom.

directions: Registered by Temple in 1992, De Colores produces large, roughly 8.5-inch spider blooms (spider ratio about 6:1) in a blend of rose, tan, and yellow, with a red-and-purple eyezone set above a strongly green throat, on 28-inch scapes. The multi-toned flower earned it the Harris Olson Spider Award in 1998 as an outstanding example of the spider form class. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Barbara Dittmer is a compact, small-flowered daylily with an extended early bloom and a tendency to rebloom.

directions: Registered by Jim Morss in 1994, Barbara Dittmer is a small-flowered (about 3.75-inch) tetraploid daylily in coral-orchid-rose-pink with a bubbly, serrated gold edge and a magenta rose eyezone above a yellow-to-green throat. It blooms early with an extended duration and frequently offers a second flush later in the season on 24-inch, semi-evergreen plants. The cultivar won the Annie T. Giles Award in 2003, the AHS honor for the most outstanding small-flowered daylily of the year. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil for best bloom.

common_name: Roses with Peaches Daylily (Small-Flowered Peach-Rose Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Roses with Peaches is a compact, small-flowered daylily blooming in early midseason.

directions: Registered by David Kirchhoff in 1991, Roses with Peaches is a small-flowered (3 to 4.5-inch), single, tetraploid daylily in peach with a gold edge, a rose eyezone, and a yellow-green throat. The 22-inch, semi-evergreen plant blooms in early midseason. It earned an Honorable Mention in 1997 before going on to win the Annie T. Giles Award in 2002 as the year's outstanding small-flowered daylily. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil for the best flower color.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; McPick is an older, small-flowered yellow daylily that is still easy to find in historic daylily collections.

directions: Introduced by George Lenington in 1957, McPick is a 24-inch, small-flowered daylily in yellow with a light rosy flush. It became one of Lenington's best-known introductions when, in 1964, it was selected as the very first winner of the newly created Annie T. Giles Award, the AHS honor for the most outstanding small-flowered daylily of the year, and it also took the Lenington All-American Award the same year. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil; this historic cultivar remains a dependable, easy-care garden plant decades after its introduction.
sources: Historical Daylilies in the Garden (Columbus Daylily Society)

common_name: Jerry Pate Williams Daylily (Melon-Pink Double Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Jerry Pate Williams is a fragrant, reblooming double daylily that may open single on its first year before settling into full double form.

directions: Registered by David Kirchhoff in 1999, Jerry Pate Williams bears large, fragrant, 5.5-inch double blooms in intense melon with a pink overlay and halo above a yellow throat, with good substance and a ruffled edge, on 25-inch scapes. It blooms early and reblooms, and newly planted divisions sometimes flower single for a season before reverting to full double form. The cultivar won the AHS Ida Munson Award for outstanding double-flowered daylily in 2005 and the Early Season Bloom Award in 2007. Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil.

common_name: Forty Second Street Daylily (Pastel Pink Double Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Forty Second Street is an evergreen, reblooming double daylily with large, pastel-toned flowers.

directions: Registered by David Kirchhoff in 1991, Forty Second Street is a large-flowered (over 4.5 inches), double, diploid daylily in pastel pink with a bright rose eyezone above a yellow-to-green throat. The 18-to-24-inch, evergreen plant blooms in midseason and reblooms for an encore performance later in the year. It won the Ida Munson Award, the AHS honor for best double-flowered daylily, in 1998. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and divide clumps every few years to keep bloom production strong.
